key_insight: SciDiagramEdit introduces a way to edit scientific figures using natural-language instructions, focusing on how figures change across paper revisions. It treats scientific diagrams as complex, structured infographics and learns to apply realistic edits such as relabeling, rearranging, and restyling.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of automating figure editing in research papers, where dense scientific diagrams contain many heterogeneous elements arranged under strict visual conventions. Existing tools struggle to understand and modify these figures from text instructions alone.
method: Builds a learning framework from paper revisions to model how scientific figures are edited over time.
Interprets natural-language edit requests and applies them to multi-element scientific diagrams with tight visual structure.
Targets common revision operations such as component relabeling, panel rearrangement, and visual restyling.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it could reduce the manual effort required to update figures during paper writing and revision. It also points toward more reliable multimodal systems for structured graphic editing in scientific workflows.
visual_elements: Before/after figure edit example showing a revised scientific diagram
Pipeline diagram of natural-language instruction -> edit understanding -> figure transformation
Annotated scientific figure with labels, arrows, panels, and captions highlighted
Workflow icon set for relabeling, rearranging, and restyling operations
paper_title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
paper_authors: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang
